sanskrit: athāsya yugam ekena caturbhiś caturo hayān ṣaṣṭhena ca śiraḥ kāyāc chareṇa rathasāratheḥ
english: With one arrow he severed Kṛpa's yoke, with four arrows he struck down his four horses, and with a sixth shaft he cut off the charioteer's head from his body.

sanskrit: tribhis triveṇuṃ samare dvābhyām akṣau mahābalaḥ dvādaśena tu bhallena cakartāsya dhvajaṃ tathā
english: With three arrows the mighty one cut the triple bamboo shaft of the chariot, with two he severed the axles, and with a twelfth broad-headed arrow he cut down Kṛpa's banner.

sanskrit: tato vajranikāśena phalgunaḥ prahasann iva trayodaśenendrasamaḥ kṛpaṃ vakṣasy atāḍayat
english: Then Phalguna, equal to Indra, as if smiling, struck Kṛpa in the chest with a thirteenth shaft that blazed like a thunderbolt.

sanskrit: sa chinnadhanvā viratho hatāśvo hatasārathiḥ gadāpāṇir avaplutya tūrṇaṃ cikṣepa tāṃ gadām
english: His bow severed, his chariot shattered, his horses slain, and his charioteer killed, Kṛpa leaped down swiftly, mace in hand, and hurled that mace.

sanskrit: sā tu muktā gadā gurvī kṛpeṇa supariṣkṛtā arjunena śarair nunnā pratimārgam athāgamat
english: But that heavy, well-adorned mace hurled by Kṛpa was deflected by Arjuna's arrows and returned along its own path.

sanskrit: tato yodhāḥ parīpsantaḥ śāradvatam amarṣaṇam sarvataḥ samare pārthaṃ śaravarṣair avākiran
english: Then warriors seeking to protect the wrathful Sharadvata's son (Kṛpa) poured showers of arrows upon Pārtha from all sides in the battle.

sanskrit: tato virāṭasya sutaḥ savyam āvṛtya vājinaḥ yamakaṃ maṇḍalaṃ kṛtvā tān yodhān pratyavārayat
english: Then Virāṭa's son (Uttara), wheeling his horses to the left and executing a twin circular maneuver, countered those warriors.

sanskrit: tataḥ kṛpam upādāya virathaṃ te nararṣabhāḥ apājahrur mahāvegāḥ kuntīputrād dhanaṃjayāt
english: Then those bull-like men, of great swiftness, took up the chariotless Kṛpa and bore him away from Kuntī's son Dhanañjaya.

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca yatraiṣā kāñcanī vedī pradīptāgniśikhopamā ucchritā kāñcane daṇḍe patākābhir alaṃkṛtā tatra māṃ vaha bhadraṃ te droṇānīkāya māriṣa
english: Arjuna said: Where that golden altar rises, resembling a blazing flame of fire, adorned with banners on its golden post — drive me there, my friend, toward Droṇa's army, blessings upon you.

sanskrit: aśvāḥ śoṇāḥ prakāśante bṛhantaś cāruvāhinaḥ snigdhavidrumasaṃkāśās tāmrāsyāḥ priyadarśanāḥ yuktā rathavare yasya sarvaśikṣāviśāradāḥ
english: His red horses shine forth — large, finely gaited, glossy as polished coral, copper-faced, lovely to behold — yoked to the finest chariot, skilled in every art of warfare.

sanskrit: dīrghabāhur mahātejā balarūpasamanvitaḥ sarvalokeṣu vikhyāto bhāradvājaḥ pratāpavān
english: Long-armed, of great splendor, possessed of strength and form, renowned in all the worlds — Bharadvaja's son (Droṇa) blazes with might.

sanskrit: buddhyā tulyo hy uśanasā bṛhaspatisamo naye vedās tathaiva catvāro brahmacaryaṃ tathaiva ca
english: In wisdom he is equal to Uśanas (Śukra), in statecraft equal to Bṛhaspati; he has mastered all four Vedas and likewise the vow of brahmacharya.

sanskrit: sasaṃhārāṇi divyāni sarvāṇy astrāṇi māriṣa dhanurvedaś ca kārtsnyena yasmin nityaṃ pratiṣṭhitaḥ
english: All the divine weapons together with their withdrawal formulas, O friend, and the entire science of archery in its completeness are ever established in him.

sanskrit: kṣamā damaś ca satyaṃ ca ānṛśaṃsyam athārjavam ete cānye ca bahavo guṇā yasmin dvijottame
english: Forbearance, self-restraint, truthfulness, non-cruelty, and uprightness — these and many other virtues reside in that best of twice-born men.

sanskrit: tenāhaṃ yoddhum icchāmi mahābhāgena saṃyuge tasmāt tvaṃ prāpayācāryaṃ kṣipram uttara vāhaya
english: I wish to fight with that greatly fortunate one in battle. Therefore, O Uttara, quickly drive me to the preceptor — urge the horses forward.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca arjunenaivam uktas tu vairāṭir hemabhūṣitān codayām āsa tān aśvān bhāradvājarathaṃ prati
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Addressed thus by Arjuna, Virāṭa's son (Uttara) urged those gold-adorned horses toward the chariot of Bharadvaja's son (Droṇa).

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ vegena pāṇḍavaṃ rathināṃ varam droṇaḥ pratyudyayau pārthaṃ matto mattam iva dvipam
english: Droṇa advanced to meet that best of chariot warriors, the Pāṇḍava, as he came on with speed — Droṇa meeting Pārtha as one maddened elephant meets another.

sanskrit: tataḥ prādhmāpayac chaṅkhaṃ bherīśatanināditam pracukṣubhe balaṃ sarvam uddhūta iva sāgaraḥ
english: Then he (Droṇa) blew his conch, which resounded like a hundred kettledrums; the entire army was agitated like a sea churned by the wind.

sanskrit: atha śoṇān sadaśvāṃs tān haṃsavarṇair manojavaiḥ miśritān samare dṛṣṭvā vyasmayanta raṇe janāḥ
english: Then men in battle marveled to see those noble red horses mingled with the swift, swan-white ones on the battlefield.

sanskrit: tau rathau vīryasaṃpannau dṛṣṭvā saṃgrāmamūrdhani ācāryaśiṣyāv ajitau kṛtavidyau manasvinau
english: Seeing those two chariots, filled with valor, at the front of the battle — the teacher and the pupil, both unconquered, both accomplished in all learning, both resolute of mind —

sanskrit: samāśliṣṭau tadānyonyaṃ droṇapārthau mahābalau dṛṣṭvā prākampata muhur bharatānāṃ mahad balam
english: — seeing Droṇa and Pārtha, both of great might, thus engaged with each other, the great army of the Bharatas trembled again and again.

sanskrit: harṣayuktas tathā pārthaḥ prahasann iva vīryavān rathaṃ rathena droṇasya samāsādya mahārathaḥ
english: And Pārtha, filled with joy, as if smiling, that heroic great chariot warrior, drew alongside Droṇa's chariot with his own.

sanskrit: abhivādya mahābāhuḥ sāntvapūrvam idaṃ vacaḥ uvāca ślakṣṇayā vācā kaunteyaḥ paravīrahā
english: Having paid obeisance, the mighty-armed son of Kuntī, slayer of enemy heroes, spoke these soothing and gentle words:

sanskrit: uṣitāḥ sma vane vāsaṃ pratikarma cikīrṣavaḥ kopaṃ nārhasi naḥ kartuṃ sadā samaradurjaya
english: "We have dwelt in the forest, wishing to repay what was done to us. You ought not be angry with us, O you who are ever unconquerable in battle."

sanskrit: ahaṃ tu prahṛte pūrvaṃ prahariṣyāmi te 'nagha iti me vartate buddhis tad bhavān kartum arhati
english: "But I shall strike only after you have struck first, O sinless one — such is the thought in my mind. May the revered one (preceptor) therefore act accordingly."

sanskrit: tato 'smai prāhiṇod droṇaḥ śarān adhikaviṃśatim aprāptāṃś caiva tān pārthaś ciccheda kṛtahastavat
english: Then Droṇa shot more than twenty arrows at him; but before they reached him, Pārtha cut them all down with practiced hand.

sanskrit: tataḥ śarasahasreṇa rathaṃ pārthasya vīryavān avākirat tato droṇaḥ śīghram astraṃ vidarśayan
english: Then the valiant Droṇa showered a thousand arrows upon Pārtha's chariot, quickly displaying his mastery of weaponry.

sanskrit: evaṃ pravavṛte yuddhaṃ bhāradvājakirīṭinoḥ samaṃ vimuñcatoḥ saṃkhye viśikhān dīptatejasaḥ
english: Thus the battle unfolded between Bharadvaja's son (Droṇa) and the diademed one (Arjuna), both releasing blazing-tipped arrows equally in the contest.

sanskrit: tāv ubhau khyātakarmāṇāv ubhau vāyusamau jave ubhau divyāstraviduṣāv ubhāv uttamatejasau kṣipantau śarajālāni mohayām āsatur nṛpān
english: Both renowned for their deeds, both equal to the wind in speed, both versed in celestial weapons, both of supreme splendor — as they hurled their nets of arrows, they bewildered even the kings.

sanskrit: vyasmayanta tato yodhāḥ sarve tatra samāgatāḥ śarān visṛjatos tūrṇaṃ sādhu sādhv iti pūjayan
english: Then all the warriors assembled there marveled, honoring them with cries of "Excellent! Excellent!" as they released their arrows with such swiftness.

sanskrit: droṇaṃ hi samare ko 'nyo yoddhum arhati phalgunāt raudraḥ kṣatriyadharmo 'yaṃ guruṇā yad ayudhyata ity abruvañ janās tatra saṃgrāmaśirasi sthitāḥ
english: "Who else but Phalguna is worthy to fight Droṇa in battle? This is the fierce dharma of the warrior class — that he fights even against his own preceptor" — so spoke the men standing at the front of the battle.

sanskrit: vīrau tāv api saṃrabdhau saṃnikṛṣṭau mahārathau chādayetāṃ śaravrātair anyonyam aparājitau
english: And those two heroes, both enraged, both great chariot warriors drawing close to each other, both undefeated, covered each other with masses of arrows.

sanskrit: visphārya sumahac cāpaṃ hemapṛṣṭhaṃ durāsadam saṃrabdho 'tha bharadvājaḥ phalgunaṃ pratyayudhyata
english: Then Bharadvaja's son, enraged, drawing his immense bow with its golden back — a bow hard to approach — fought back against Phalguna.

sanskrit: sa sāyakamayair jālair arjunasya rathaṃ prati bhānumadbhiḥ śilādhautair bhānoḥ pracchādayat prabhām
english: With nets of arrows, whetted on stone and blazing with light, launched toward Arjuna's chariot, he covered even the radiance of the sun.

sanskrit: pārthaṃ ca sa mahābāhur mahāvegair mahārathaḥ vivyādha niśitair bāṇair megho vṛṣṭyeva parvatam
english: And that great chariot warrior, the mighty-armed one, pierced Pārtha with swift, sharp arrows, as a cloud pierces a mountain with rain.

sanskrit: tathaiva divyaṃ gāṇḍīvaṃ dhanur ādāya pāṇḍavaḥ śatrughnaṃ vegavad dhṛṣṭo bhārasādhanam uttamam visasarja śarāṃś citrān suvarṇavikṛtān bahūn
english: Likewise the Pāṇḍava, taking up his divine Gāṇḍīva bow — that supreme instrument of bearing the burden of battle, the enemy's destroyer, swift as the wind — boldly released many varied arrows fashioned with golden decorations.

sanskrit: nāśayañ śaravarṣāṇi bhāradvājasya vīryavān tūrṇaṃ cāpavinirmuktais tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: Destroying Bharadvaja's son's showers of arrows with shafts quickly loosed from his bow, the valiant one performed what seemed like a wonder.

sanskrit: sa rathena caran pārthaḥ prekṣaṇīyo dhanaṃjayaḥ yugapad dikṣu sarvāsu sarvaśastrāṇy adarśayat
english: Dhanañjaya, Pārtha, moving in his chariot — a splendid sight to behold — simultaneously displayed all his weapons in every direction.

sanskrit: ekacchāyam ivākāśaṃ bāṇaiś cakre samantataḥ nādṛśyata tadā droṇo nīhāreṇeva saṃvṛtaḥ
english: He made the sky like a single shadow with arrows on all sides; Droṇa was not visible at that moment, covered as if by a mist.

sanskrit: tasyābhavat tadā rūpaṃ saṃvṛtasya śarottamaiḥ jājvalyamānasya yathā parvatasyeva sarvataḥ
english: His form at that moment, enveloped by those finest of arrows blazing all around, was like a mountain blazing with fire on all sides.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā tu pārthasya raṇe śaraiḥ svaratham āvṛtam sa visphārya dhanuś citraṃ meghastanitanisvanam
english: But seeing his own chariot covered by Pārtha's arrows in battle, Droṇa drew his wondrous bow, whose sound was like the rumbling of thunder clouds,

sanskrit: agnicakropamaṃ ghoraṃ vikarṣan paramāyudham vyaśātayac charāṃs tāṃs tu droṇaḥ samitiśobhanaḥ mahān abhūt tataḥ śabdo vaṃśānām iva dahyatām
english: — terrible as a wheel of fire — drawing that supreme weapon to its fullest, that glorious one in battle, Droṇa, shattered those arrows; and then there arose a great sound like that of bamboos burning.

sanskrit: jāmbūnadamayaiḥ puṅkhaiś citracāpavarātigaiḥ prācchādayad ameyātmā diśaḥ sūryasya ca prabhām
english: With arrows whose nocks were made of refined gold, issuing from that excellent and decorated bow, the immeasurable-souled one covered the directions and the brilliance of the sun.

sanskrit: tataḥ kanakapuṅkhānāṃ śarāṇāṃ nataparvaṇām viyaccarāṇāṃ viyati dṛśyante bahuśaḥ prajāḥ
english: Then those gold-nocked arrows with their smooth joints, flying through the sky, were seen in great numbers by the people — filling the heavens.

sanskrit: droṇasya puṅkhasaktāś ca prabhavantaḥ śarāsanāt eko dīrgha ivādṛśyad ākāśe saṃhataḥ śaraḥ
english: The arrows issuing from Droṇa's bow, clinging together nock to nock, appeared in the sky as a single long, continuous arrow.

sanskrit: evaṃ tau svarṇavikṛtān vimuñcantau mahāśarān ākāśaṃ saṃvṛtaṃ vīrāv ulkābhir iva cakratuḥ
english: Thus those two heroes, releasing great arrows adorned with gold, made the sky as if covered with meteors.

sanskrit: śarās tayoś ca vibabhuḥ kaṅkabarhiṇavāsasaḥ paṅktyaḥ śaradi khasthānāṃ haṃsānāṃ caratām iva
english: And their arrows, feathered with heron and peacock plumes, shone like lines of swans moving through the autumn sky.

sanskrit: yuddhaṃ samabhavat tatra susaṃrabdhaṃ mahātmanoḥ droṇapāṇḍavayor ghoraṃ vṛtravāsavayor iva
english: A fierce, terrible battle arose there between those two great souls, Droṇa and the Pāṇḍava, like the battle between Vṛtra and Vāsava (Indra).

sanskrit: tau gajāv iva cāsādya viṣāṇāgraiḥ parasparam śaraiḥ pūrṇāyatotsṛṣṭair anyonyam abhijaghnatuḥ
english: And like two elephants approaching each other and striking with the tips of their tusks, they struck each other with arrows released at full draw.

sanskrit: tau vyavāharatāṃ śūrau saṃrabdhau raṇaśobhinau udīrayantau samare divyāny astrāṇi bhāgaśaḥ
english: Those two heroes, both enraged and resplendent in battle, fought each other, invoking their divine weapons in sequence.

sanskrit: atha tv ācāryamukhyena śarān sṛṣṭāñ śilāśitān nyavārayac chitair bāṇair arjuno jayatāṃ varaḥ
english: Then Arjuna, the foremost among the victorious, warded off with sharp arrows those stone-whetted shafts released by the chief of preceptors.

sanskrit: darśayann aindrir ātmānam ugram ugraparākramaḥ iṣubhis tūrṇam ākāśaṃ bahubhiś ca samāvṛṇot
english: Displaying himself, Indra's son (Arjuna), fierce and of fierce valor, swiftly covered the sky with many arrows.

sanskrit: jighāṃsantaṃ naravyāghram arjunaṃ tigmatejasam ācāryamukhyaḥ samare droṇaḥ śastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ arjunena sahākrīḍac charaiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ
english: Droṇa, the chief of preceptors, the best of weapon-bearers, sported with Arjuna in battle — even as Arjuna, that tiger among men of blazing splendor, sought to slay him — playing with arrows of smooth-jointed shafts.

sanskrit: divyāny astrāṇi muñcantaṃ bhāradvājaṃ mahāraṇe astrair astrāṇi saṃvārya phalgunaḥ samayodhayat
english: Against Bharadvaja's son releasing divine weapons in the great battle, Phalguna countered weapon with weapon and fought him equally.

sanskrit: tayor āsīt saṃprahāraḥ kruddhayor narasiṃhayoḥ amarṣiṇos tadānyonyaṃ devadānavayor iva
english: The collision of those two lions among men, both enraged, both intolerant of each other, was like the clash of gods and demons.

sanskrit: aindraṃ vāyavyam āgneyam astram astreṇa pāṇḍavaḥ droṇena muktaṃ muktaṃ tu grasate sma punaḥ punaḥ
english: The Pāṇḍava absorbed with his own weapon, again and again, the Aindra (Indra's), the Vāyavya (wind-god's), and the Āgneya (fire-god's) weapons as Droṇa released them one after another.

sanskrit: evaṃ śūrau maheṣvāsau visṛjantau śitāñ śarān ekacchāyaṃ cakratus tāv ākāśaṃ śaravṛṣṭibhiḥ
english: Thus those two heroes, those great bowmen, releasing sharp arrows, made the sky like a single shadow with their showers of shafts.

sanskrit: tato 'rjunena muktānāṃ patatāṃ ca śarīriṣu parvateṣv iva vajrāṇāṃ śarāṇāṃ śrūyate svanaḥ
english: Then, as Arjuna's arrows were released and fell upon living bodies, there was heard the sound of those shafts — like thunderbolts falling upon mountains.

sanskrit: tato nāgā rathāś caiva sādinaś ca viśāṃ pate śoṇitāktā vyadṛśyanta puṣpitā iva kiṃśukāḥ
english: Then, O lord of the people, elephants, chariots, and horsemen, drenched in blood, were seen like blossoming kimshuka trees.

sanskrit: bāhubhiś ca sakeyūrair vicitraiś ca mahārathaiḥ suvarṇacitraiḥ kavacair dhvajaiś ca vinipātitaiḥ
english: And with arms still bearing their armlets, with great chariot warriors fallen, with golden and variegated armor and with banners brought down —

sanskrit: yodhaiś ca nihatais tatra pārthabāṇaprapīḍitaiḥ balam āsīt samudbhrāntaṃ droṇārjunasamāgame
english: — and with warriors slain there, tormented by Pārtha's arrows, the army was thrown into turmoil at the clash of Droṇa and Arjuna.

sanskrit: vidhunvānau tu tau vīrau dhanuṣī bhārasādhane ācchādayetām anyonyaṃ titakṣantau raṇeṣubhiḥ
english: But those two heroes, brandishing their bows — those instruments for bearing the burden of battle — covered each other with arrows, enduring the shafts of war.

sanskrit: athāntarikṣe nādo 'bhūd droṇaṃ tatra praśaṃsatām duṣkaraṃ kṛtavān droṇo yad arjunam ayodhayat
english: Then there arose a sound in the sky from those praising Droṇa: "Droṇa has accomplished a feat hard to perform — that he fought against Arjuna."

sanskrit: pramāthinaṃ mahāvīryaṃ dṛḍhamuṣṭiṃ durāsadam jetāraṃ devadaityānāṃ sarpāṇāṃ ca mahāratham
english: "That agitator of all, of great valor, firm of fist, hard to approach, the conqueror of gods, demons, and serpents, that great chariot warrior —"

sanskrit: aviśramaṃ ca śikṣāṃ ca lāghavaṃ dūrapātitām pārthasya samare dṛṣṭvā droṇasyābhūc ca vismayaḥ
english: And seeing Pārtha's ceaseless skill, swiftness, and ability to shoot at distant targets in battle, Droṇa too was filled with wonder.

sanskrit: atha gāṇḍīvam udyamya divyaṃ dhanur amarṣaṇaḥ vicakarṣa raṇe pārtho bāhubhyāṃ bharatarṣabha
english: Then, O bull of the Bharatas, the intolerant Pārtha, taking up his divine Gāṇḍīva bow, drew it with both arms in battle.

sanskrit: tasya bāṇamayaṃ varṣaṃ śalabhānām ivāyatam na ca bāṇāntare vāyur asya śaknoti sarpitum
english: His rain of arrows, like an extending swarm of locusts — even the wind could not pass through the gaps between those shafts.

sanskrit: aniśaṃ saṃdadhānasya śarān utsṛjatas tadā dadṛśe nāntaraṃ kiṃ cit pārthasyādadato 'pi ca
english: No interval whatsoever was seen in Pārtha at that moment, whether he was nocking arrows ceaselessly, releasing them, or taking them up again.

sanskrit: tathā śīghrāstrayuddhe tu vartamāne sudāruṇe śīghrāc chīghrataraṃ pārthaḥ śarān anyān udīrayat
english: And so, while that terrible battle of swift weapons proceeded, Pārtha released yet more arrows — faster than fast.

sanskrit: tataḥ śatasahasrāṇi śarāṇāṃ nataparvaṇām yugapat prāpataṃs tatra droṇasya ratham antikāt
english: Then hundreds of thousands of arrows with smooth joints descended upon Droṇa's chariot simultaneously from close range.

sanskrit: avakīryamāṇe droṇe tu śarair gāṇḍīvadhanvanā hāhākāro mahān āsīt sainyānāṃ bharatarṣabha
english: As Droṇa was being showered by the arrows of the Gāṇḍīva-bearer, O bull of the Bharatas, a great cry of "Ah! Ah!" rose from the troops.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavasya tu śīghrāstraṃ maghavān samapūjayat gandharvāpsarasaś caiva ye ca tatra samāgatāḥ
english: Maghavan (Indra) honored the Pāṇḍava's swift weaponry, and so did the gandharvas, the apsaras, and all who had assembled there.

sanskrit: tato vṛndena mahatā rathānāṃ rathayūthapaḥ ācāryaputraḥ sahasā pāṇḍavaṃ pratyavārayat
english: Then Aśvatthāmā, the son of the preceptor, commander of a chariot division, suddenly checked the Pāṇḍava with a great multitude of chariots.

sanskrit: aśvatthāmā tu tat karma hṛdayena mahātmanaḥ pūjayām āsa pārthasya kopaṃ cāsyākarod bhṛśam
english: Yet Aśvatthāmā in his heart honored the feat of the great-souled Pārtha, even as he aroused in himself great anger.

sanskrit: sa manyuvaśam āpannaḥ pārtham abhyadravad raṇe kirañ śarasahasrāṇi parjanya iva vṛṣṭimān
english: He, overcome by rage, charged at Pārtha in battle, showering thousands of arrows like a rain-laden thundercloud.

sanskrit: āvṛtya tu mahābāhur yato drauṇis tato hayān antaraṃ pradadau pārtho droṇasya vyapasarpitum
english: But the mighty-armed Pārtha, turning his horses toward where Droṇa's son (Aśvatthāmā) was, gave Droṇa an interval to withdraw.

sanskrit: sa tu labdhvāntaraṃ tūrṇam apāyāj javanair hayaiḥ chinnavarmadhvajaḥ śūro nikṛttaḥ parameṣubhiḥ
english: And Droṇa, having gained that interval, quickly departed with his swift horses — that hero, his armor and banner cut down, himself struck by the finest arrows.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca taṃ pārthaḥ pratijagrāha vāyuvegam ivoddhatam śarajālena mahatā varṣamāṇam ivāmbudam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Pārtha received him (Aśvatthāmā) — rising like a gust of wind, pouring arrows like a cloud — with a great net of arrows.

sanskrit: tayor devāsurasamaḥ saṃnipāto mahān abhūt kiratoḥ śarajālāni vṛtravāsavayor iva
english: Their great clash, both of them hurling nets of arrows, was like the meeting of gods and demons — like the clash of Vṛtra and Vāsava.

sanskrit: na sma sūryas tadā bhāti na ca vāti samīraṇaḥ śaragāḍhe kṛte vyomni chāyābhūte samantataḥ
english: The sun did not shine at that moment, nor did the wind blow, as the sky was made dense with arrows and became shadow all around.
